Duly authorized agents of the city shall have access at all hours to the premises of the consumer for the purpose of installing or removing city property, inspecting piping, reading and testing meters, or for any other purpose in connection with the water service and its facilities.
(1) Extensions to the system shall be made only when the consumer shall cause to be granted or conveyed to the city a permanent easement of right-of-way across any property traversed by the water and sewer lines.
(2) The city will pay for any main extensions within the limits of the city.
(3) The city water mains will be extended only to areas that have been proven feasible for extension.
(4) In situations where a consumer or potential consumer requests service outside of the existing service area of the city water system, the city will consider the request. If it is determined not to be feasible economically for the city to extend its service, the consumer or potential consumer can, at his own expense, extend the service area under the following guidelines:
a. All cost for materials and construction will be paid by the consumer or potential consumer.
b. All extensions will be made with six-inch or larger Class 200 Schedule 40 pipe.
c. All pipeline put in the ground will have to comply with city specifications and be inspected prior to backfilling.
d. The consumer or potential consumer understands and agrees that once the extension is connected to the city water system, the extension then becomes city property and the consumer or potential consumer has no right or claim to the extension or revenues derived from the extension.
e. The consumer or potential consumer must submit the plans for the proposed extension to the city's engineer; the cost of the study and report by the engineer will be the responsibility of the consumer or potential consumer.
Once the city engineer has approved the plans, the city council will consider the expansion of the city's system to include same.
(Comp. Ords. 2001, § 17.15; Ord. of 4-13-2004)
700:
Not less than three days' notice must be given, in person or in writing, at the city clerk's office to discontinue water and sewer service or to change occupancy.
(1) In the event of sale of property to which water and/or sewer service is provided and payment for such service is in delinquent status, service to the seller shall not be provided at any new location, or if currently served at another location, such service shall be discontinued, until any delinquent bill is paid.
(2) A new owner of property to which water and/or sewer service has previously been provided shall apply for service within 48 hours after occupying the premises, and failure to do so will make him liable for paying for services (water and sewer) since the last meter reading.
(3) When a consumer moves from one location to another and both are served by the city water system, a transfer fee will be charged according to a fee schedule on file in the office of the clerk.
(Comp. Ords. 2001, § 17.16)
701:
Utility bills, including charges for water, leak insurance, sewer, fire and solid waste shall be mailed out on such dates as may be determined as desirable by the city. Bills shall be paid at the city clerk's office and are due upon the due date shown on the bill. The failure to receive bills or notices shall not prevent such bills from becoming delinquent or relieve the consumer from payment of same. The failure of water and/or sewer users to pay charges duly imposed shall result in the automatic imposition of the following cumulative penalties:
(1) Nonpayment by the due date shown on the bill shall result in imposition of a penalty of ten percent of the delinquent amount, including all services provided by the city.
(2) Nonpayment of the entire outstanding balance within ten days after the due date on the bill shall result in the bill being placed on the list for disconnections of service without further notice. The city will disconnect the service and a seal belonging to the city will be attached to the meter.
(3) If service has been disconnected for nonpayment of the outstanding balance, service will be restored only after the outstanding balance is paid in full including a reconnection fee. The reconnection fee is set by council.
(4) If the cut-off seal is removed by the consumer, the city shall have the right and authority to issue an arrest warrant for the consumer for the theft of services and destruction of city property, and charge a fee for removal of the seal, or other damage, as determined by the city, or its designee.
(Comp. Ords. 2001, § 17.17; Ord. of 8-9-2016, § 17.17; Ord. of 8-10-2016)
702:
When water and sewer service is discontinued and all bills paid, the security deposit shall be refunded to the consumer by the city.
(1) Upon discontinuance of service for nonpayment of bills, the security deposit will be applied by the city toward the settlement of the account. Any balance will be refunded to the consumer; however, if the security deposit is insufficient to cover the bill, the city may proceed to collect the balance in the usual way provided by the law for collection debts.
(2) The city reserves the right to discontinue its services without notice for the following additional reasons:
a. Prevention of fraud or abuse.
b. Consumer's willful disregard of the city's rules.
c. Emergency repairs.
d. Insufficiency of water supply due to circumstances beyond the control of the city.
e. Legal processes.
f. Direction of public authorities.
g. Strike, riot, fire, flood, or unavoidable accident.
(Comp. Ords. 2001, § 17.18; Ord. of 8-9-2016, § 17.18)
703:
If the consumer believes his bill to be in error, he shall present his claim, in person, at the office of the city clerk before the bill becomes delinquent. Such claim, if made after the bill has become delinquent, shall not be effective in preventing discontinuance of service as heretofore provided. The consumer may pay such bill under protest, and said payment shall not prejudice his claim.
(1) The city will make a special water meter reading at the request of the consumer.
(2) Water meter will be tested at the request of the consumer upon payment to the city of the actual costs of making the test; provided, however, that if the meter is found to over-register beyond three percent of the correct volume, no charge will be made for such test.
(3) If the seal of a meter is broken by other than the city's representatives, or if the meter fails to register correctly, or is stopped for any cause, the consumer shall pay an estimated amount from the record of his previous bills and/or from other proper data.
(4) Unless otherwise provided by leak insurance protection, there will be no water adjustments resulting from excessive water consumption resulting from a leak in the customer's service line.
(Comp. Ords. 2001, § 17.19; Ord. of 8-9-2016, § 17.19)
707:
(a) The director of the department of public works or his designee is authorized to discontinue water service to prevent contamination/pollution of the public water supply/system, due to possible cross-connections, or when necessary to protect the water supply/system or individual properties from emergency cross-connections or backflow situations.
(b) The department of public works and/or building inspections department are further authorized to install, or require to be installed, suitable backflow prevention devices at the customer's/owner's service connections or other areas as needed to prevent contamination or the risk thereof for the public water system.
(c) The department of public works and building inspections department shall reserve the right to periodically inspect and test any backflow prevention devices. Installation, testing, and repairs shall be in accordance with the department of public works backflow prevention by containment policy and procedures. Inoperative or faulty devices shall be promptly repaired/replaced by the customer/owner or the water service shall be terminated.
(Ord. No. 130, § I, 5-9-1995)
708:
In addition to other penalties provided by this Code, further punishment shall include restitution for the following:
(1) The total cost incurred by the city to repair or replace facilities damaged as a result of the violation;
(2) Any injury or damage to persons or property and/or loss of services resulting from the violation.
(Ord. No. 130, § II, 5-9-1995)
709:
Qualifying customers may purchase, as an addition to the normal rates of charge implemented by the city, protection against excessive leaks caused by any and all types of defects that might exist as a result of an inordinate, unusual, or non-customary amount of water being used by a customer. Costs of this coverage shall be as established by the city from time to time.
(Ord. No. 330, § 1, 11-13-2007)
711:
The term "exigent circumstances" is defined, for purposes of interpretation of this policy, to mean circumstances beyond the control and reasonable foreseeability of a customer. An example of personal exigent circumstances would include, but not be limited to, a customer's death, disability, stroke, serious accident or illness, or inability to reside in the customer's home for some period of time, which renders it impractical for the customer to determine and control the use of water at the residence. In addition to personal exigent circumstances, the term "exigent circumstances" may also include, but not be limited to, technical problems, inordinate water usage that could not be discovered, failure of piping, infrastructure, or water conservation use devices, detection devices, or similar circumstances which warrant an additional adjustment by the council. The council shall have the right to make adjustments based upon improper calculation of the leak reduction amount pursuant to section 36-46.
(Ord. No. 330, § 3, 11-13-2007)
712:
The method for calculating a leak adjustment for excessive use shall be as follows:
(1) An average of six months' water usage, for the period not involved in the leak, which normally will be the six-month period prior to discovery of the leak, shall be calculated. In the event the customer has had water service for less than six months, then the average monthly billing either just before the leak, and just after the leak shall be calculated, so as to either meet the six months' requirement, or as nearly as practicable determine the appropriate average six months' charge. A leak adjustment covers no more than two consecutive months of excessive water use.
(2) The rate of charge shall then represent the average water usage for the preceding six months, excluding the month billing cycle in which the leak occurred, not to exceed $500.00. Leak insurance customer claims may not exceed $500.00 in a 12-month period beginning with an initial claim. Any amount over $500.00 per 12-month period is not covered under the leak insurance policy.
(3) Any person who disputes the billing methodology and does not have exigent circumstances that might justify additional billing concessions may appeal the accounting methodology to the council. The decision of the council in the accounting method for determining the average bill to be paid shall be final.
(4) Any customer may request an additional leak concession, in charges to be made to that customer, based upon exigent circumstances as defined in section 36-45. All appeals to the council making a customer's claim for exigent circumstances must be in writing, set forth the grounds for the claim, and shall be heard by the council within 60 days of the appeal. No appeal shall be considered if not filed within 90 days of the date of final adjustment accomplished by the council pursuant to the normal adjustment policy set forth in this section.
(Ord. No. 330, § 5, 11-13-2007; Ord. No. 330, 8-25-2011)
713:
No customer shall be entitled to an adjustment as a result of a leak that causes an inordinate or excessive amount of water usage if he has not purchased the leak protection described herein. Further, no claim on a customer's leak insurance plan will be processed in the first six months of the coverage period when leak insurance protection was not purchased at the time of the initial water connection.
(Ord. No. 330, § 6, 11-13-2007)
714:
All bill adjustment requests must be approved by the council for consideration.
(Ord. No. 330, § 7, 11-13-2007)
715:
The protection offered by this policy shall only be available to residential customers with single meters who use a smaller volume of water, and churches. Multifamily, multi-users, multiple mobile homes, or commercial customers shall not be eligible for leak insurance coverage.
(Ord. No. 330, § 8, 11-13-2007)
716: No connection to city water distribution lines will be permitted unless and until any water lines connected to a private well are completely disconnected from the lines connecting to the city water system.
717:
Water furnished by the city shall be used for consumption by the consumer, members of his household, and employees only, and the consumer shall not sell water to any other person or permit any other person to use said water. Water shall not be used in a manner which would interfere with the regular domestic consumption in the area served. Disregard of this rule shall be sufficient cause for refusal and/or discontinuance of service.
(1) Where a meter or meter box cannot be installed in the right-of-way, the meter or meter box may be placed on the premises of a consumer, in a suitable place, as determined by the city, and the consumer, property owner, and their agents shall provide unobstructed access at all times to the meter reader.
(2) When a consumer's meter is not located within the public right-of-way or when the meter is located within the boundaries of the consumer's property, the consumer shall be responsible for all repair to that line except for the part on the public right-of-way. The city will maintain the meter.
(3) The consumer's piping and apparatus, beyond the connection place provided by the city, shall be installed and maintained by the consumer at the consumer's expense, in a safe and efficient manner, and in accordance with the sanitary regulations of the state health department.
(4) The consumer is responsible for granting the city an easement when any part of the water system's property is located on the property of the consumer.
(5) The consumer is liable for any negligent damage to the property of the water system of the city.
(6) In order to be received as a consumer and entitled to receive water from the city's water system, all applicants must show that any private wells located on their property are not physically connected to the lines of the city's water system, and all applicants, by becoming consumers of the city, covenant and agree that so long as they continue to be consumers of the city, they will not permit the connection of any private wells on their property to the water system of the city. The consumer must not connect the city's water system to any other form of water supply.
(7) If one meter is currently serving several premises or dwelling units having a common owner, the landlord or owner shall be considered the city's consumer and shall be billed accordingly and shall be responsible for the water service.
(8) After the enactment of the ordinance from which this article is derived, no meter shall be used for multiple service to serve several different premises, and each household, dwelling unit, or other premises shall be served by a separate meter.
(9) A separate meter must be installed for irrigation systems.
(Comp. Ords. 2001, § 17.14)
720:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Aquifer means a geologic formation, group of formations, or a part of a formation that is capable of yielding water to a well.
Dewatering well means any well withdrawing 100,000 gallons of groundwater or less on any one day in order to remove groundwater from the vicinity of an excavation and which extends at least 50 feet into the earth or at least ten feet below the water table, whichever is greater.
Groundwater means waters of underground streams, channels, artesian basins, reservoirs, lakes or other water under the surface of the earth.
Individual water well means any well constructed for the purpose of obtaining groundwater appurtenant to a single-family dwelling and intended for public use, including, but not limited to, household purposes, farm livestock or gardens.
Industrial well means any well constructed for the purpose of withdrawing 100,000 gallons of groundwater or less on any one day for processing or cooling water or for purposes other than drinking water.
Irrigation well means any well constructed for the purpose of obtaining groundwater to supply irrigation water for agriculture or land beautification, but excluding single-family irrigation of lawns or gardens.
Monitoring well means any well for which the primary purpose is to collect data for hydrologic, geohydrologic or groundwater quality or quantity evaluations.
Water well means any excavation which is cored, bored, drilled, jetted, dug or otherwise constructed for the purpose of withdrawing groundwater and which is intended or usable as a source of water supply for individual homes, farms, irrigation, industrial processes, public water systems or non-public water systems.
(Ord. No. 160, art. I, 11-9-1999)
721:
(a) It shall be unlawful, except as hereinafter provided, to construct or maintain any water well in the city, except as provided herein.
(b) The owners of all houses, buildings or properties used for human occupancy, employment, recreation or other persons situated within the city are hereby required, at their expense, to install water lines thereon, and to connect such facilities directly with the city's public water system, within 90 days of official notice to do so, provided that said public water is within 100 feet (30½ meters) of the property line and access is available over public land.
(Ord. No. 160, art. II, 11-9-1999)
722:
(a) Private water wells in the city limits may not be used for residential consumption. Water wells for irrigation purposes may be used with council approval.
(b) Any water well shall not in any manner affect the aquifer that provides the water for the city's public water system, directly or indirectly.
(c) No water well shall be operated until the installation is completed to the satisfaction of the city. The city shall be allowed to inspect the work at any stage of construction.
(Ord. No. 160, art. III, 11-9-1999)
723:
Nothing contained herein shall prohibit the city from selling wholesale untreated water to any person.
(Ord. No. 160, art. IV, 11-9-1999)
727:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) means the quantity of oxygen utilized in the biochemical oxidation of organic matter under standard laboratory procedure in five days at 20 degrees Celsius, expressed in milligrams per liter.
Building drain means that part of the lowest horizontal piping of a drainage system which receives the discharge from soil, waste, and other drainage pipes inside the walls of the building and conveys it to the building sewer, beginning five feet (1½ meters) outside the inner face of the building wall.
Building sewer means the extension from the building drain to the public sewer or other place of disposal.
Combined sewer means a sewer receiving both surface runoff and sewage.
Garbage means solid wastes from the domestic and commercial preparation, cooking, dispensing of food, and from the handling, storage, and sale of produce.
Industrial wastes means the liquid wastes from industrial manufacturing processes, trade, or business as distinct from sanitary sewage.
Natural outlet means any outlet into a watercourse, pond, ditch, lake, or other body of surface water or groundwater.
Person means any individual, firm, company, association, society, corporation, or group.
pH means the logarithm of the reciprocal of the weight of hydrogen ions in grams per liter of solution.
Properly shredded garbage means the wastes from the preparation, cooking, and dispensing of food that have been shredded to such a degree that all particles will be carried freely under the flow conditions normally prevailing in public sewers, with no particle greater than one-half inch (1.27 centimeters) in any dimension.
Public sewer means a sewer in which all owners of abutting properties have equal rights, and is controlled by public authority.
Sanitary sewer means a sewer which carries sewage and to which stormwaters, surface waters, and groundwaters are not intentionally admitted.
Sewage means a combination of the water-carried wastes from residences, business buildings, institutions, and industrial establishments, together with such groundwaters, surface waters, and stormwaters as may be present.
Sewage treatment plant means any arrangement of devices and structures used for treating sewage.
Sewage works means all facilities for collecting, pumping, treating, and disposing of sewage.
Sewer means a pipe or conduit for carrying sewage.
Slug means any discharge of water, sewage, or industrial waste which in concentration of any given constituent or in quantity of flow exceeds for any period or duration longer than 15 minutes more than five times the average 24-hour concentration or flows during normal operation.
Storm drain or storm sewer means a sewer which carries stormwaters and surface waters and drainage, but excludes sewage and industrial wastes, other than unpolluted cooling water.
Superintendent means the superintendent of sewage works and/or of water pollution control of the city or his authorized agent or representative, or other designated agency.
Suspended solids means solids that either float on the surface of, or are in suspension in, water, sewage, or other liquids, and which are removable by laboratory filtering.
Watercourse means a channel in which a flow of water occurs, either continuously or intermittently.
(Ord. No. 100, art. I, 7-9-1991)
728:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to place, deposit, or permit to be deposited in any unsanitary manner on public or private property within the city or in any area under the jurisdiction of the city, any human or animal excrement, garbage, or other objectionable waste.
(b) It shall be unlawful to discharge to any natural outlet within the city, or in any area under the jurisdiction of the city, any sewage or other polluted waters, except where suitable treatment has been provided in accordance with subsequent provisions of this article.
(c) Except as hereinafter provided, it shall be unlawful to construct or maintain any privy, privy vault, septic tank, cesspool, or other facility intended or used for the disposal of sewage.
(d) The owners of all houses, buildings, or properties used for human occupancy, employment, recreation, or other purposes situated within the city and abutting on any street, alley, or right-of-way in which there is now located or may in the future be located a public sanitary or combined sewer of the city are hereby required, at their expense, to install suitable toilet facilities therein, and to connect such facilities directly with the proper public sewer in accordance with the provisions of this article, within 90 days after date of official notice to do so, provided that said public sewer is within 100 feet (30½ meters) of the property line and access is available over public land.
(Ord. No. 100, art. II, 7-9-1991)
